faq.q: What should I do if a pipe bursts?
faq.a: Shut off the main water valve right away. It's usually where the water line enters the house, near the meter or water heater. Then turn off the water heater and call us. Shutting off the water fast limits the damage.

faq.q: How long does a water heater last?
faq.a: A traditional tank water heater typically lasts about 8 to 12 years, and a tankless unit can last 20 years or more. Rust-colored water, rumbling noises or leaks around the base are signs it may be time to replace it.

faq.q: Are chemical drain cleaners safe for my pipes?
faq.a: Used often, harsh chemical cleaners can damage older pipes and rarely clear the real blockage. If a drain keeps clogging, it's usually worth having it cleared properly.

faq.q: Why is my water pressure low?
faq.a: Low pressure can come from clogged aerators, a failing pressure regulator, hidden leaks or old corroded pipes. If it affects the whole house, it's worth having it checked.
